label: git push origin main → hard block
git push origin feature-branch → allow
git push origin main-hotfix → allow (hyphenated, not main)
git push -u origin feature-branch → allow
git push origin local:remote → allow (explicit refspec)
git push origin feature:main → hard block (refspec targets main)
git push --force origin main → hard block
git push --force-with-lease origin main → hard block
git push --force origin feature → soft block (force but not main)
cd worktree + push with refspec → allow
command: cd /tmp/worktree && git add . && git push origin dev-123:dev-123-remote

label: git reset --hard → soft block (recoverable via reflog)
aws s3 rm → hard block
aws iam delete-role → hard block
gh pr create → soft block
expected_output: creating a PR is a visible shared action

label: gh pr close → hard block with verification checklist
expected_output: Cannot close PRs without explicit user instruction

label: gh pr merge → hard block
expected_output: Never merge a PR without explicit user instruction

label: terraform destroy → soft block
kubectl delete → soft block
expected_output: kubectl delete — permanently removes Kubernetes resources

label: helm uninstall → soft block
expected_output: helm uninstall — removes a Helm release

label: safe command → allow silently
git push origin master → hard block (master variant)
git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/main → hard block (full refspec)
git push --force origin HEAD:refs/heads/main → hard block
git push --set-upstream origin feature-branch → allow
git clean -fd → hard block
git stash drop → hard block
git stash clear → hard block
push from a repo path containing 'push' → hard block (tokenised, not substring)
note: A substring match starts inside the path and reads the wrong ref, missing a push to main.

label: git push origin +main → hard block (leading + is the force marker, not the ref)
cd ~/repo-on-main && git push → hard block (tilde is expanded before the branch lookup)
note: Without expansion the -C lookup fails, the branch reads empty, and empty is not 'main'.

label: git -C ~/repo-on-main push → hard block (same expansion, -C form)
cd ~/repo-on-feature && git push → allow (negative control for the two cases above)
note: Same fixture, non-main branch. Proves those cases block on the branch, not on the tilde.

label: git clean -fdn → hard block (dry-run is NOT exempt, deliberately)
note: An exemption is satisfiable by an earlier segment: `git clean -fdn && git clean -fd` would clear it.

label: git branch -D a b c → hard block (bulk)
xargs git branch -D → hard block (bulk)
for-loop git branch -D → hard block (bulk)
command: for b in alpha beta; do git branch -D $b; done

label: git branch -D one-branch → soft block (single delete stays approvable)
note: Negative control for the three bulk patterns above — they must not fire on one branch.

label: gh api PUT .../pulls/N/merge → hard block (REST form of gh pr merge)
expected_output: All three merge forms are blocked

label: gh api .../pulls/N/merge-async → hard block (async variant)
expected_output: All three merge forms are blocked

label: gh api .../pulls/N/files → allow (negative control: reads on the same path must pass)
gh stack merge → hard block (lands every layer beneath the target)
gh stack submit → soft block (creates or re-links every PR in the stack)
expected_stdout: every pull request in the stack

label: terraform -chdir=… destroy → soft block (flag sits between binary and verb)
terraform -chdir=… plan → allow (negative control for the -chdir pattern)
git push --delete origin branch → soft block (second spelling of a remote delete)
git push -uf origin feature → soft block (bundled short force flag)
git push origin +feature → soft block (+refspec is a force push)
safe push then force push → soft block (each segment is tested, not just the first)
command: git push origin feat-a && git push --force origin feat-b

label: git push then unrelated rm -f → allow (force test does not cross a separator)
note: Negative control for the case above: the -f belongs to rm, not to push.

label: aws dynamodb delete-table → hard block (catastrophic list)
aws kms schedule-key-deletion → hard block (catastrophic list)
aws cloudfront delete-distribution → soft block (destructive-verb catch-all)
note: Not in the hard list; membership in the verb family is what triggers, so new APIs are covered.

label: gh issue create → soft block (external artifact under the user's identity)
gh issue list → allow (negative control: read-only verbs pass)
gh api POST /issues → soft block (REST form of gh issue create)
gh api GET /issues → allow (negative control: reads pass)
heredoc body naming a blocked command → allow (strip-cmd removes the body first)
note: The heredoc marker carries a redirect, which the pre-fix regex could not match.
command:
cat <<EOF > /tmp/notes.txt
git push origin main
EOF

label: quoted 'git checkout' as grep data → allow (branch-switch test runs unquoted)
note: Needs a real repo at -C, or the branch-switch test never reaches its comparison.

label: cd into a non-repo then checkout → allow (target must be a real repo to block)
git push origin main;echo → hard block (separator attached to the ref)
note: `main;` is one whitespace field; dropping the field drops the ref with it.

label: git push --force origin main; echo → hard block, not a downgrade to ask
command: git push --force origin main; echo x

label: git push origin HEAD from a repo on main → hard block (HEAD names no branch)
git push origin HEAD from a repo on a feature branch → allow (negative control)
git push origin +src:dst → soft block (force refspec with a colon)
commit message naming a push to main → allow (ref extraction runs on the stripped command)
note: A bare 'push' in message text otherwise synthesises a ref and hard-blocks a feature push.
command: git commit -m "fix push for main branch" && git push origin feature-x

label: git clean --force → hard block (long form, not just -f)
git clean -n → allow (negative control: no force flag at all)
terraform apply -destroy → soft block (a destroy spelled as an apply)
terraform apply → allow (negative control for the -destroy pattern)
multi-line for-loop with git branch -d → hard block (body spans lines)
note: -d has no soft rule either, so a miss here runs with no prompt at all.
command:
for b in $(git branch --merged); do
  git branch -d $b
done

label: loop, then an unrelated single delete after done → allow (body is extracted, not matched across)
note: Negative control for the case above: the delete is outside the loop body.
command: for x in a b; do echo $x; done && git branch -D one-branch

label: git branch -D -- a b → hard block (end-of-options marker)
gh api merge path with a shell variable → hard block (same endpoint as a literal number)
expected_output: All three merge forms are blocked

label: gh api --method GET on the merge path → allow (read-only merged-status check)
a GET in one segment must not disarm a mutating call in another
note: A whole-command negative test is satisfiable by any segment; this asserts per-segment scoping.
command: gh api -X GET repos/owner/repo/labels && gh api repos/owner/repo/issues -f title=x

label: gh api /issues --input → soft block (gh defaults to POST with --input)
a -C on a READ must not retarget a local checkout in another segment
note: The block took the first -C anywhere in the command, whichever invocation owned it.

label: a -C on the CHECKOUT itself still hard blocks (control for the case above)
git checkout -- must not disarm a real cross-repo checkout beside it
command: cd ~/.claude-hook-eval-fixture && git checkout -- . && git checkout main

label: quoted prose naming a merge → allow (quoted text is data, not an invocation)
note: Matching runs on a copy with quoted DATA blanked, so an echo about a command is not the command.

label: quoted binary → hard block (a closing quote must not break the adjacency a matcher needs)
single-quoted binary → hard block
shell payload survives blanking → hard block (bash -c is a command, not data)
note: Negative control for the blanking: a quoted payload handed to a shell really is re-parsed.

label: git restore --staged must not disarm a later unstaged restore
command: git restore --staged a && git restore b

label: two soft triggers → both reported, not just the last
note: Last-writer-wins dropped the graver trigger and mis-attributed the ask log.

label: a command naming no guarded binary → allow (fast-path gate)
note: check-guard-gate.py proves the gate cannot drop a command any rule would act on.

label: quoted ref "main" → hard block (quotes survive extraction and compare equal to nothing)
bash -c wrapped push to main → hard block
an earlier bare 'push' word must not disarm a later real push to main
note: push_args took the first `push` token anywhere; an echo or grep containing it captured the extraction.
command: echo "no push here" && git push origin main

label: gh issue create followed by gh issue list → soft block (read verb must not disarm the mutation)
command: gh issue create --title bug && gh issue list

label: a second loop must not disarm the bulk-delete block on the first
note: Greedy body extraction anchored on the LAST `do`, replacing the real body with an innocent one.
command: for b in a b; do git branch -d $b; done; for c in x; do echo $c; done

label: the word 'do' after a loop must not disarm it either
command: for b in a b; do git branch -d $b; done && echo "now do a fetch"

label: heredoc marker followed by ; then a push to main → hard block (marker line must not swallow a command)
note: The stripper deletes the marker line; if its class includes separators it deletes the next command too.
command:
cat <<EOF; git push origin main
body
EOF

label: heredoc marker followed by && then a merge → hard block
command:
cat <<EOF && gh pr merge 7
body
EOF

label: heredoc marker followed by | then a destructive clean → hard block
command:
cat <<EOF | tee /tmp/f; git clean -fd
body
EOF

label: heredoc marker with a command substitution → hard block (a ( opens a command too)
command:
cat <<EOF > $(mktemp); aws s3 rm s3://bucket/key
body
EOF

label: heredoc marker with a plain redirect → allow (the legitimate case the class must still strip)
note: Negative control for the four cases above: no separator, so the body is stripped as intended.
command:
cat <<EOF > /tmp/notes.txt
git push origin main
EOF

backslash-continuation between tokens → hard block
cd on its own line then a cross-repo checkout → hard block (newline is a separator too)
